items.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: Jerome Kern when he finished “All The Things You Are” said I’ve just written a classic.

ctx.x: That’s interesting. The opposite may happen sometime. You may write something that you just think is the best —

Oh that has happened. That’s happened more often than the other way around. You kind of say wow. And then you give it to somebody and they say, “That’s nice,” you know. And so I mean I don’t know whether we ever really know or can tell, or whether I can, other people can I’m sure. But you wonder if — Jerome Kern when he finished “All The Things You Are” said I’ve just written a classic. This is going to be the greatest, one of the great songs ever, and it’s perfect. Or whether he just thought well I did that one…

You wonder if they, how jazz musicians, why they’ve chosen certain songs to latch on to like that. I mean it seems to be perfect for improvising and the whole thing, but like you said, he may have had no idea that that was going to happen with that particular tune.
